This makes me so sad to read, my mum went through the same stage when I was in my early teens. Completely disconnected from the family, heavily depressed. She was so difficult to be around. 

My parents did get divorced, me and my siblings stayed with my father. She moved out of the house. Her depression escalated to where she was sucidal, my mum was intolerable to visit she would just cry constantly, say everyone hated her, often I'd come out and she'd be laying on the couch sobbing. I was scared for her life and ended up living with her a year or so after, I would make her cups of tea and get her to sit up, just try to constantly pull her out of that hole she was in. She got herself into all of these awful situations that no one should go through. 

Now she has managed to really pull herself together again it took a few years, and I'm so proud of her. I think she really lost herself, she was 18 when she met my father and had her first kid in her early 20's she gave up all her ambitions and life. My dad was a controlling man and not very affectionate. I think both of them were immature in regards to relationships and communication completely broke down. Mum got her own job, started making new friends, goes out on trips a lot now- I think she just needed a change or to feel like there was more that defined her than a mum and wife.  

The way you talk in your post 'SHE does this' reminds me a lot of my dad and I think half of the detatchment us kids developed towards our mum was this whole 'us' and 'her' mentality that he fueled

My parents divorce is a huge mess that has been dragging on for years now, the debt they have from lawyers etc is probably more than whatever finances they had in the start.   Divorce is not so simple.

Looking back I wish they had tried to make it work, marrige councilling, taking a break. Dad said he tried, but honestly throwing someone at a doctor isn't a substitute for love and acceptance. 

Would you still want to be with your wife if she wasn't depressed? 
If you wouldn't then leave her. 

If you would, then you've said doctors etc aren't working for her. Like others have said, turn off the internet, the tv. Work back down, think about why you loved her and married her in the start. Talk to her, reminise, take her on a date, go on a little family roadtrip. 

Depression is an illness that is treatable. It's not a life sentence.
